title: Stop Using RAG as Memory — Daniel Chalef, Zep
talk_summary: Chalef argues that generic fact-extraction into a vector store produces semantically similar but business-irrelevant memories, and that agents need developer-defined domain schemas (entities, fields, business rules) stored in a temporal graph so retrieval can filter by type. The demo registers Pydantic/Zod/Go-struct schemas with Zep, which then extracts typed business objects (financial goals, debts, income) that tools query concurrently with node-type filters.

takeaways.technique: Schema-typed memory instead of raw fact vectors
takeaways.what_they_do: Developers declare domain entity types with fields and value rules (Pydantic/Zod/Go structs) and register them; the memory layer extracts only those typed objects, and retrieval filters by node type rather than pure semantic similarity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: semantic similarity is not business relevance

takeaways.what_they_do: A single agent tool runs multiple filtered memory searches concurrently and returns one 'snapshot' object rather than the agent issuing many sequential retrievals.
takeaways.evidence_quote: retrieve a financial snapshot which runs multiple zep searches at the same time concurrently and filters by specific node types

takeaways.what_they_do: Entity fields carry validation rules so extracted values are constrained at write time, keeping memory clean rather than post-filtering garbage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can even define fields, the business rules for those fields
